Sam (acct:acme-inc): hey team — we've got a bunch of 4xxs from the /v1/rerank endpoint since last night. Some requests return 404 'model not found', others return 200 but the scores are all 0.0. breaking prod flows. can someone look?

Priya S. (Support): sorry you're seeing that, Sam. can you paste a trimmed request and the exact model_id you used? also which region/tenant?

Sam (acct:acme-inc): sending now. tenant: acme-prod-us, region: us-west-2. used model_id: rerank-v1-legacy-2022. request:```POST /v1/rerank
Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "rerank-v1-legacy-2022",
  "input": [
    {"id": "q1","text": "best noise cancelling headphones"},
    {"id": "c1","text": "Bose QuietComfort 45 - comfortable, good noise canceling"},
    {"id": "c2","text": "Sony WH-1000XM5 - slightly pricier, excellent ANC"}
  ]
}
```response (trimmed):```HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{
  "results": [
    {"id":"c1","score":0.0},
    {"id":"c2","score":0.0}
  ]
}
```also sometimes it's 404: ```HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found
{"error":"model id 'rerank-v1-legacy-2022' not found or deprecated"}
```

Priya S. (Support): thanks. two paths: either the model was deprecated/removed (404 path) or there's a routing mismatch causing a fallback to a placeholder scorer that returns zeros. i've opened an escalation to eng-ml. @Diego M. can you pick this up?

Jules (support-bot): Incident created: #INC-20260315-1287 linked to this thread.

Diego M. (Eng-ML): looking. quick q: do you have the request_id header from one of the failing calls? that helps trace through the routing layer. if not, a timestamp window is fine.

Sam (acct:acme-inc): i can pull logs. one example request_id: req_8b7a2c. timestamp ~ 2026-03-14T23:12:07Z.

Diego M. (Eng-ML): thanks. preliminary check: our model registry had a deprecation entry for rerank-v1-legacy-2022 last month and we moved traffic to rerank-v2-stable. but customers with pinned model ids should still serve. i'm going to check alias mapping for acme-prod-us and if there's an accidental purge.

Priya S. (Support): another note — customer reported this started after a config rollout last night (autoscaler/traffic routing changes) so could be related.

Diego M. (Eng-ML): found something. the tenant's per-tenant mapping used an internal alias 'rerank-default' -> 'rerank-v2-stable'. but our per-tenant override table had a stale entry: 'rerank-v1-legacy-2022' mapped to empty string due to a bad migration. that explains the 404. the zero scores path is likely because when no model is mapped we fall back to NullScorer which returns zeros.

Sam (acct:acme-inc): that matches what we see — some calls hit an older routing node that still referenced the legacy id (404), others hit the fallback scorer (0s). any ETA? this is blocking our search rerank feature.

Diego M. (Eng-ML): fixing mapping now. quick patch to the tenant mapping store to remap rerank-v1-legacy-2022 -> rerank-v2-stable for acme-prod-us. will roll to canary then prod. patch script:```# remap alias
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/tenant-mapping/acme-prod-us \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer internal-REDACTED' \
  -d '{"model_map":{"rerank-v1-legacy-2022":"rerank-v2-stable"}}'```rolling in 2 mins. i'll post when done.

IncidentsBot: Change scheduled: tenant-mapping update for acme-prod-us at 2026-03-15T00:02:00Z — initiated by diego.

Priya S. (Support): Sam — i'll monitor and ping you as soon as traffic returns to normal. also adding a temp customer note recommending to use model alias 'rerank-default' in requests to avoid pinned IDs.

Diego M. (Eng-ML): deployed the mapping change to 3 canary nodes. doing test calls now.

Diego M. (Eng-ML): test results: canary nodes now return non-zero scores and expected rank order. example:```{
  "results":[{"id":"c2","score":0.78},{"id":"c1","score":0.42}]
}```

Sam (acct:acme-inc): i see improved responses for that req_8b7a2c timeframe. thanks. any chance some older nodes still have the stale config?

Diego M. (Eng-ML): yes one remaining region node had cached mapping. will force cache invalidation across routing layer. running:```POST /internal/cache/invalidate
{ "keys": ["tenant:acme-prod-us:mappings"] }```should finish in ~5m.

Priya S. (Support): Sam — quick heads up on follow-ups we've added to the ticket: 1) full audit of migration that introduced empty mapping, 2) add validation to control-plane to prevent empty-string mappings, 3) SDK warning when pinned model ids are deprecated, and 4) recommend customers migrate to alias-based usage.

Diego M. (Eng-ML): cache invalidation complete. all nodes returning proper scores now. i'm leaving a postmortem note for the migration change causing empty mapping. root cause: a database migration script treated missing legacy entries as deletion and set value to "" for some tenants. fix: deploy migration rollback + validation.

Sam (acct:acme-inc): confirmed — our production traffic looks stable and re-rank results restored. thanks to everyone. do you have an ETA for the SDK warning? we'd prefer early detection on our side.

Priya S. (Support): we requested the SDK team for a patch — scoped as a minor release that checks model id against the deprecation list and logs a clear warning when used. aiming for next week. i'll share PR link when available.

Diego M. (Eng-ML): also adding a safe-fail behavior: if model_id maps to empty, return 409 with a descriptive error instead of silently using NullScorer. that will ship in the next runtime patch.

IncidentsBot: Incident #INC-20260315-1287 resolved by diego; status: mitigated.

Priya S. (Support): closing loop — i've updated the incident with mitigation steps and customer timeline. Sam, if you want a follow-up postmortem summary emailed, i can send it. :thumbsup:

Sam (acct:acme-inc): yes please. appreciate the quick turn. :heart:

Diego M. (Eng-ML): leaving action items in the incident: - rollback bad migration script - add validation to control-plane write path - runtime: return 409 for empty mapping - SDK: deprecation warning - monitor: add alert when NullScorer traffic > 1%

Priya S. (Support): marking this resolved on support side. re-open if anything else pops up.

Sam (acct:acme-inc): will do. thanks again!
